T1110.name: Brute Force
T1110.description: Repeatedly guessing passwords or credentials to gain unauthorized access to an account.

T1078.name: Valid Accounts
T1078.description: Using legitimate, stolen, or compromised credentials to gain or maintain access, often to blend in with normal activity.

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol
T1071.description: Using standard protocols like HTTP or DNS to communicate with a command-and-control server, hiding traffic among normal network activity.

T1003.name: OS Credential Dumping
T1003.description: Extracting stored credentials, password hashes, or authentication tokens from an operating system.

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
T1059.description: Abusing tools like PowerShell, cmd.exe, or bash to execute commands and scripts on a system.

T1021.name: Remote Services
T1021.description: Using legitimate remote access services like SSH or RDP to move laterally between systems on a network.
